title: Frequency adverbs: daily life in the plaza

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *siempre*, *a veces* and *nunca*, and from B1 Unit 12 *normalmente*, *a menudo*, *de vez en cuando* and *cada día*. In a description of colonial life they go with the imperfect, which tells how things used to happen.

items.spanish: Normalmente, los vecinos iban a la plaza para comprar comida.
items.english: Normally, the residents went to the plaza to buy food.

items.spanish: A menudo, los vendedores llegaban de los pueblos vecinos.
items.english: Often, the sellers came from the neighbouring towns.

items.spanish: Cada día, el mercado era un lugar de trabajo y de noticias.
items.english: Every day, the market was a place of work and news.

items.spanish: De vez en cuando había fiestas para celebrar la llegada de un virrey.
items.english: From time to time there were festivals to celebrate the arrival of a viceroy.

sections.content: Put the adverb at the start or before the verb, and use the imperfect for habits in the past: *iban*, *llegaban*, *había*. With *nunca* after the verb you need *no*: *no había nunca*.
